review: PR #1: camera input parity with the source Three.js r128 OrbitControls behaviour

verifiedSemantics: dampingFactor 0.06 applied per update to the pending spherical/pan delta and remainder retained 0.94
perspective pan uses 2*radius*tan(fov/2)/clientHeight along the camera right/up columns; target damped by 0.06 with 0.94 retention
wheel is sign-only and uses dollyIn=scale*0.95 / dollyOut=scale/0.95 with radius clamped to 4..180
modifier remap: ROTATE+ctrl/meta/shift -> PAN; PAN+ctrl/meta/shift -> ROTATE; MIDDLE -> DOLLY
touch modes: one finger rotate, two fingers dolly (pinch ratio) + pan, one-finger/two-finger page coordinates

browserEvidence.environment: headless Chrome 155 + real WebGPU, 754x424 canvas, demo FAB
notes: The first-visit onboarding overlay was dismissed before gesture dispatch (it covers the canvas).
Camera pose was read from the product ?perf bridge (getCameraPose), so changes are real scene-camera changes, not DOM-only assertions.

followUpFixes: Forwarded the orbit updater's already-clamped spherical radius to the Lite camera adapter (879c519) so limit values stay exact (180.00000000000003 -> 180); the frozen lite-camera limit assertions now pass.
knownBoundaries: Input was synthesized through CDP mouse/touch events in headless Chrome; physical devices, Safari/iOS touch behaviour and pen input were not tested.
No side-by-side visual/pixel comparison against the original Three.js build was performed; parity was verified against the r128 source semantics plus real-camera kinematics in the Lite scene.
The render performance gate was not re-run for this PR; the probe observed a rendering scene with no GPU errors, and the existing dev/60Hz gates remain available for follow-up.

PR #1 was merged locally into main (merge commit c1d1678) because this session has no GitHub CLI/API credentials; mark the Draft PR merged/closed in the GitHub UI (or via API) if the remote PR state matters.
